summary: Analysis of 14 days of telemetry data shows optimal glycemic outcomes with 99.7% Time in Range (70–180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), and a mean glucose of 117.0 mg/dL (CV 12.9%). Active basal rates, carb ratios, sensitivity factors, and AAPS oref1 automated delivery operate seamlessly together to maintain stable nocturnal euglycemia and effective meal recovery.

analysis_steps.findings: 1,345 CGM entries across 14 days provide complete 100% data coverage with zero gaps. Active AAPS profile and treatment data are fully documented.
analysis_steps.evidence: Coverage 100%, 0 gaps, cadence estimated at 15 minutes, 28 meal/insulin treatment logs available.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic variability is very low (CV 12.9%) with zero severe hyperglycemia (>250 mg/dL) and zero time spent below 70 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 99.7%, TAR 0.3%, TBR 0.0%, average glucose 117.0 mg/dL, minimum glucose 70 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal rates accurately maintain overnight glucose stability within target ranges (90–115 mg/dL) without upward drift or hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight local mean glucose sits steadily between 103 and 107 mg/dL from 00:00 to 05:00.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb Ratios and ISF settings are well-calibrated. Postprandial peaks return to baseline within 4 hours without late-phase insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: +240 min glucose deltas across all logged meals remain between -11 and +8 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Automated SMB and UAM features complement meal boluses effectively, preventing extreme spikes without causing post-meal hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true; postprandial glucose peaks remain <=188 mg/dL and resolve safely.

analysis_steps.findings: AAPS safety limits (Max Basal 2.4 U/h, Max IOB 8.0 U) provide sufficient headroom for standard meals while protecting against excessive accumulation.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max Basal is ~2.3x maximum profile basal (1.05 U/h); Max IOB accommodates peak meal insulin demands.

analysis_steps.findings: User-declared meal bolus timing (20-min prebolus for weekday breakfast, 10-min for weekend brunch) yields predictable postprandial curves.
analysis_steps.evidence: 10 breakfast entries and 4 brunch entries demonstrate reproducible 2-hour peaks followed by complete 4-hour recovery.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared e-carbs (20g over 120m) for weekend brunch effectively manage delayed glycemic rises from mixed/higher-fat meals.
analysis_steps.evidence: Brunch glucose peaks at ~188 mg/dL at +120 min and returns to 115 mg/dL by +240 min without hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.findings: All profile and automation parameters demonstrate high alignment with observed glycemic patterns. No profile or parameter adjustments are indicated.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 99.7%, zero hypoglycemia, steady overnight fasting lines, and resolved meal curves across 14 days.

strengths: Exceptional Time in Range of 99.7% with 0.0% time below 70 mg/dL.
Highly stable overnight fasting glucose averaging 103–107 mg/dL.
Low glycemic variability with a standard deviation of 15.1 mg/dL and CV of 12.9%.
Effective integration of oref1 SMB/UAM with user meal strategies across fast and mixed carb entries.

recommendations.title: Maintain Current Profile and Automation Settings
recommendations.description: Telemetry confirms that basal rates, carb ratios, ISF, DIA, and AAPS safety parameters are optimally configured. No changes are recommended.

profile_recommendation.rationale: All profile parameters across basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and targets produce outstanding glycemic stability (99.7% TIR, 0% TBR, CV 12.9%).
profile_recommendation.next_check: Re-evaluate telemetry in 30 days or if daily routines or meal compositions change significantly.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Maintain all current basal rates, carb ratios, ISF, DIA, and target segments unchanged.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight glucose remains flat and stable at 103-107 mg/dL with zero hypoglycemia.
Maintains euglycemia through morning fasting and pre-meal intervals.
Provides stable afternoon baseline glucose control between meals.
Supports evening stability and smooth transition into nocturnal sleep.
No late-night meal boluses show under- or over-bolusing trends.
Effectively covers weekday breakfast carbs with complete 4-hour recovery.
Accurately covers weekend brunch meals alongside e-carb strategy.
Dinner boluses reliably return glucose to baseline without postprandial rises.
Overnight corrections and loop adjustments remain safe and effective.
Morning sensitivity factor aligns well with dynamic loop corrections.
Afternoon corrections restore euglycemia cleanly without overshooting.
Evening sensitivity supports safe SMB delivery after dinner.
Nighttime target range maintains optimal euglycemic baseline.
Daytime target range provides strong control without hypoglycemia risk.
Bedtime target range safely cushions sleep onset.
5.5-hour duration of insulin action matches observed decay curves.
SMB and UAM operate safely to minimize postprandial excursions.
Source raw settings contained null values for individual activation toggles; active delivery is safe and verified in execution.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Standard oref1 delivery settings provide smooth dosing without insulin stacking.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Limits provide effective safety guardrails relative to total daily insulin requirements.
100% sensitivity adjustment factor is stable; specific Autosens boolean toggles contain null in export and can be verified on device.
Carbohydrate absorption settings accurately model meal decay across all logged entries.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: For standard fast-carb meals, administer a 20-minute prebolus with a 70% immediate bolus split, letting SMB/UAM handle minor absorption variations. For mixed, higher-fat weekend brunch meals, use a 10-minute prebolus with a 60% immediate bolus and log 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes (15-min start offset).
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: This strategy prevents early postprandial spikes while matching the slower absorption tail of complex meals, achieving 99.7% Time in Range without hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Confirm exact food start time relative to bolus entry during weekend brunch to verify if postprandial peak timing is driven by fat delay or prebolus length.

exceptions.suggestion: 10-min prebolus, 60% immediate bolus, 20g e-carbs over 120 min starting +15 min.
exceptions.rationale: Smooths out the delayed glycemic peak (~188 mg/dL) caused by higher fat and protein content.

implementation_steps: Review current telemetry outcomes with the diabetes care team.
Maintain all active profile basal rates, carb ratios, ISF, DIA, and target segments.
Continue standard 20-minute prebolus execution for fast-carb weekday meals.
Continue entering e-carbs for higher-fat/protein weekend brunch meals as currently practiced.
education: Time in Range above 99% with 0% hypoglycemia indicates excellent alignment between basal insulin, carb ratios, and automated loop responsiveness.
Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) inform AAPS oref1 logic to expect delayed absorption, allowing SMB and UAM to safely deliver gradual insulin over 2 to 4 hours.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice.
The user must independently verify all settings and discuss prospective changes with their healthcare provider.
Always make parameter adjustments one at a time and monitor glucose closely following any system modification.
